extracted.intended_audience: Title IX Coordinators and education institution administrators (K-12 and postsecondary), and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Title IX Coordinators on when and how to initiate a complaint (grievance procedures) in the absence of a complainant, after withdrawal, or following termination of informal resolution. Includes enumerated factors to consider, required notifications, and limits on initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's request not to proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant's request not to proceed with initiation of a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(1) incorporates the complainant's request as a required factor; a recipient should honor a complainant's request not to proceed when doing so is consistent with the recipient's obligation to operate its education program free from sex discrimination. The request is one of the minimum considerations and may weigh against initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's reasonable safety concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant's reasonable safety concerns regarding initiation of a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(2) (and (vi)) require Title IX Coordinators to weigh reasonable safety concerns as paramount. The Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant before initiating a complaint and appropriately address reasonable safety concerns (e.g., offering escorts, other protective measures). This consideration may counsel against initiation or require mitigation steps if initiation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of additional acts if complaint not initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: The risk that additional acts of sex discrimination would occur if a complaint is not initiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether there have been other reports or complaints about the respondent or a pattern of behavior suggesting risk of future discrimination. This factor weighs in favor of initiation when it indicates an ongoing or escalating threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity of the alleged sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The severity of the alleged sex discrimination, including whether the discrimination, if established, would require removal of a respondent or imposition of other disciplinary sanctions to end the discrimination and prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks July 2022 NPRM discussion of seriousness (violent acts, threats, use of a weapon, retaliation). Severity that might require removal or serious sanctions supports initiation to protect health/safety and prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and relationship of the parties; respondent employee status
rubrics_metrics.description: The age and relationship of the parties, including whether the respondent is an employee of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for power imbalances (e.g., employee-student) or other relational dynamics that may increase risk or justify initiation. Employee status of respondent may make initiation more likely to address affected workplace or learning environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the alleged conduct (pattern or multiple impacted individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the alleged sex discrimination, including information suggesting a pattern, ongoing sex discrimination, or sex discrimination alleged to have impacted multiple individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether allegations implicate broader, systemic, or repeated conduct (including multiple victims) that would implicate the rights of numerous individuals and justify grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of evidence to assist a decisionmaker
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of evidence to assist a decisionmaker in determining whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies Title IX Coordinators are not making a determination of whether discrimination occurred; lack or unavailability of evidence may weigh against initiating a complaint when the complainant has not elected to proceed. Still, Title IX Coordinators must comply with obligations to take other appropriate prompt and effective steps under final §106.44(f)(1)(vii) if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether recipient can end discrimination without grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the recipient could end the alleged sex discrimination and prevent its recurrence without initiating grievance procedures under §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator should consider alternative mechanisms (e.g., collective bargaining remedies, policy/practice changes) that could remedy the problem; if effective, this may counsel against initiating Title IX grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold standard for initiation (imminent serious threat or prevention of equal access)
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering the enumerated factors and other relevant information, a Title IX Coordinator must determine that the conduct as alleged either (a) presents an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of the complainant or other person, or (b) prevents the recipient from ensuring equal access on the basis of sex to its education program or activity; otherwise the Title IX Coordinator must not initiate a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified in final §106.44(f)(1)(v)(B). These two considerations are the limiting standard—initiation is permitted only in these narrow circumstances. The Coordinator may decline to initiate if post-allegation events (e.g., respondent resignation or transfer) ameliorate health/safety or equal access concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and addressing safety before initiating without complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Title IX Coordinator initiates a complaint under paragraph (f)(1)(v), the Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant prior to doing so and appropriately address reasonable concerns about the complainant's safety or the safety of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(f)(1)(vi) requires prior notice and reasonable safety measures when initiating over a complainant's wishes; examples include offering escorts or other protections. The notice ensures the complainant can raise safety concerns and that the Coordinator can mitigate risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial assessment is a threshold determination 'as alleged', not a credibility finding
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator's initial assessment under §106.44(f)(1)(v) is a threshold determination required to satisfy Title IX obligations and is not a credibility determination or an assessment of whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator must consider information 'as alleged' (consistent with final §106.2 definitions). The assessment uses available information and is not an investigation or fact-finding that decides responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other relevant information; enumerated factors are minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: The enumerated factors are minimum considerations; a Title IX Coordinator may consider other relevant information known to them when deciding whether to initiate a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final text permits reliance on Coordinator's experience, knowledge from prior complaints, or other pertinent facts. The factors do not preclude consideration of additional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions required when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, a Title IX Coordinator must take the actions set out under paragraphs (f)(1); these actions are required unless the Coordinator reasonably determines under paragraph (f)(2) that the conduct as alleged could not constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that prompt actions (including consideration of initiation) attach only when the conduct 'reasonably may' constitute sex discrimination. The Coordinator's specialized knowledge is authorized to assess plausibility and whether further action under Title IX is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator must take 'other appropriate prompt and effective steps' to end sex discrimination in addition to considering initiation of grievance procedures when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and a response is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules narrow and clarify proposed §106.44(f)(6): such steps are required when the Coordinator assesses the information and determines it describes conduct that could constitute sex discrimination. Recipients have flexibility to choose appropriate measures outside grievance procedures, but must ensure nondiscriminatory access and prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No initiation based on mere suspicion or to avoid liability
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator must not initiate a complaint based on mere suspicion or misunderstanding, nor be encouraged to initiate complaints solely to avoid possible legal liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states the regulation is not intended to create a low bar for initiation; Coordinators should use the enumerated factors and the threshold test to avoid inappropriate or speculative initiation. Initiation should be fact-specific and limited to the narrow circumstances described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent/legal representative involvement and deference
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent, legal guardian, or authorized legal representative must be permitted to exercise whatever rights they have under state/local law to act on behalf of a complainant or other person; Title IX Coordinator may consult parents and generally should defer to parent wishes for minors except in cases of serious threat to the health or safety of the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As explained in §106.6(g), parents may make complaints, accompany minors to proceedings, and otherwise participate. Deference to parents is appropriate unless there is a serious health/safety threat requiring action to protect the child; the Coordinator may still need to take other steps to ensure equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedure protections apply to Coordinator-initiated complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator-initiated complaint is investigated and resolved under the recipient's grievance procedures, and the procedural protections of §§106.45 (and if applicable 106.46) apply to all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes that initiation by a Coordinator does not remove due process or other procedural rights of respondents or complainants; grievance procedures afford a fair process regardless of who initiated the complaint.
